newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Boral to supply gas to Murrin Murrin mine.
newsitem.headline: Boral to supply gas to Murrin Murrin mine.

text.p: The Boral Energy arm of Boral Ltd has reached an agreement to supply gas to the Murrin Murrin nickel and cobalt mining project in Western Australia, the management company for the project said on Wednesday.
The agreement is for a minimum 16 years with a value of A$220 million, Murrin Murrin Operations Pty Ltd said.
Murrin Murrin Operations is the manager of the project for Anaconda Nickel Ltd and Glencore International AG.

As part of the agreement, Boral would build, own and operate an 80-kilometre spur line from an outlet point west of Leonora on the Goldfields Gas Transmission/Kalgoorlie pipeline to Murrin Murrin, the company said.
Gas would be sourced from the Carnarvon Basin offshore of Western Australia, Murrin Murrin said.
The A$900 million Murrin Murrin project is located east of the outback town of Leonora in Western Australia.
Murrin Murrin is scheduled to come on stream at the end of 1998 and to reach production of 45,000 tonnes of nickel and 3,000 tonnes of cobalt in that year.
Glencore International AG of Switzerland, which has a 40 percent stake in Murrin Murrin and a 19 percent stake in Anaconda Nickel, has exclusive rights to sell the cobalt and nickel.
Anaconda has plans to expand annual production to 75,000 tonnes of nickel and 5,000 tonnes of cobalt once the base plant is commissioned.
